title: Check yourself: reading what a request carries

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A participant reads the POS entry mode with Integer.parseInt(request.getString(22)), inside a try with catch (ISOException e). An e-commerce purchase arrives without field 22. What does the client that sent it get?

options.text: A response with 30, since the TransactionManager answers for a participant that fails in prepare
options.says: the TransactionManager logs a warning and counts the vote as ABORTED; it builds no response

options.text: A response with 96, since SendResponse builds a system error when it runs on the abort path
options.says: SendResponse only sends what is under RESPONSE; with nothing there it sends nothing

options.text: No response, since the transaction aborts before the participant has put anything under RESPONSE
options.says: parseInt(null) throws a NumberFormatException the catch doesn't cover, the vote counts as ABORTED, and SendResponse has nothing to send

options.text: No response, since the session that ran the participant stops and the request stays in the queue
options.says: the TransactionManager catches the exception and the session carries on with the abort path

origin.section: 6.1 A Missing Field Reads as `null`, and a Participant That Throws Answers Nobody

questions.stem: A participant checks hasField(4), converts field 4 with Long.parseLong and approves anything up to 30000 cents. Both ends use iso87ascii.xml. A purchase arrives whose field 4 reads -00000004000. What happens to it?

options.text: It is approved, since the value parseLong returns is below the limit
options.says: parseLong accepts a leading sign, so -4000 passes the limit check; only a digits check would refuse it

options.text: It is refused with 30, since parseLong rejects a sign in a numeric field
options.says: parseLong accepts a leading minus or plus sign

options.text: It never reaches the participant, since the server's packager rejects the minus sign
options.says: the ASCII numeric field packager checks the length, not the characters

options.text: It never reaches the participant, since the client's packager refuses to pack it
options.says: the client's packager doesn't look at the characters either; the field goes out as it was set

origin.section: 6.2 A Numeric Field Is Text That Nobody Checked

questions.stem: A limit participant divides field 4 by 100 for every currency. Its limits are 1,000,000 won (410, a currency with no minor unit) and 400.000 Kuwaiti dinars (414, a currency with three decimals). One purchase arrives with field 4 = 000003000000 in won, another with field 4 = 000000350000 in dinars. What does the participant answer?

options.text: It approves the won purchase and declines the dinar one, since it reads 30,000 won and 3,500 dinars
options.says: the won has no minor unit and the dinar has three decimals, so dividing by 100 shrinks one and inflates the other

options.text: It declines the won purchase and approves the dinar one, since it reads 3,000,000 won and 350 dinars
options.says: those are the real amounts; reading them needs each currency's decimals, which dividing by 100 ignores

options.text: It approves both purchases, since dividing by 100 makes every amount smaller than it is
options.says: for a currency with three decimals, dividing by 100 makes the amount ten times larger than it is

options.text: It declines both purchases, since dividing by 100 makes every amount larger than it is
options.says: for a currency without a minor unit, dividing by 100 makes the amount a hundred times smaller

origin.section: 6.3 An Amount Counts the Minor Units of the Currency in Field 49

questions.stem: A participant declines a purchase, sets field 44 of its response to a 30-character reason from the core system, puts the response in the Context and votes ABORTED. The server's layout is iso87ascii.xml, where field 44 holds up to 25 characters. What reaches the terminal?

options.text: The decline with field 44 cut to 25 characters, since the packager shortens a value that is too long
options.says: the packager refuses a value that is too long; it never shortens it

options.text: The decline without field 44, since the packager leaves out a field it can't pack
options.says: a field that can't be packed makes the whole pack fail; nothing is sent

options.text: Nothing, since the pack fails inside SendResponse and the channel logs that send with the error under it
options.says: set accepts any length; the packager checks when SendResponse sends, after the vote, and the channel's log shows a send that never left

options.text: Nothing, since set refuses the text and the exception leaves prepare before the response is in the Context
options.says: set checks nothing; the value is stored and only fails when the message is packed

origin.section: 6.5 `set` Checks Nothing; the Packager Checks After the Vote

concepts: A response that fails to pack is logged by the channel as a send with the error under it, while the TransactionManager's event shows a clean transaction.
A missing field reads as null; a participant that throws while reading it gets an ABORTED vote and leaves no response, so the client gets nothing.
